name: the famous one
description: The sound Czech is famous for. The tongue tip vibrates as for a rolled r, but the tongue is raised and tense, so you also hear a buzz like the s in pleasure. It is one sound, not r followed by zh.
tip: Start from a strong rolled r and raise the front of your tongue until it buzzes. After p, t and k, and at the end of a word, ř loses its voice and hisses.

name: r and l as vowels
description: Between two consonants, r and l can carry a syllable on their own. That is why Czech has words with no vowel letters.
tip: Do not add a vowel before the r or l. Hold the r or l for the length of a short vowel instead.

name: sh as in shoe
tip: Round the lips a little and draw the tongue back from the teeth.

name: ch as in chat
tip: It is t and š said as one sound.

name: s as in pleasure
description: Like the s in pleasure, or the j in French bonjour.
tip: At the end of a word it loses its voice and sounds like š.

name: ts as in cats
description: Always ts, as at the end of cats, even at the start of a word. Never k, never s.
tip: Say cats, then drop the ca.

name: ch as in loch
description: The sound in Scottish loch or German Bach. Czech treats ch as a single letter, and it comes after h in the alphabet.
tip: Make a k, then let air hiss through the gap instead of closing it.

name: a voiced h
description: A voiced, breathy h, deeper than English h. It is never silent.
tip: At the end of a word it turns into ch: mlh ends in the ch sound.

letters: Ď ď · Ť ť · Ň ň
name: ď, ť and ň
description: Soft consonants, made with the middle of the tongue against the roof of the mouth. Ň is like the ni in onion. Before i, í and ě, plain d, t and n are soft too.
tip: Ti in svišti is the same sound as ť: the t softens before i.

name: ě
description: Not a vowel of its own. It is e that changes the consonant before it: bě, pě, vě, fě sound like bje, pje, vje, fje; dě, tě, ně sound like ďe, ťe, ňe; mě sounds like mňe.
tip: Read the consonant and ě together as one unit.

letters: á é í ý ó ú ů
name: long vowels
description: The accent mark shows a long vowel, not stress. Length can change the meaning of a word. Í and ý sound the same, as do ú and ů.
tip: Stress always falls on the first syllable, whether it is long or short.
